BSc Psychology is an undergraduate course that studies human behaviour, emotions, thought processes, learning, memory and social interaction. It uses scientific methods to understand why people behave differently in different situations.

Students commonly study areas such as cognitive psychology, developmental psychology, social psychology, biological psychology, research methods and statistics. Depending on the university, the course may include laboratory activities, surveys, case analysis, field visits, projects or internships.

This degree can be a foundation for careers in research, human resources, education, community support and behavioural services. However, professional roles such as clinical psychologist or counselling psychologist generally require postgraduate education, supervised training and any registration required by the relevant authority.

chunks.text: Typical eligibility Completion of Class 12 or an equivalent qualification. Many institutions accept Science, Commerce and Humanities students. A minimum percentage may apply. Some universities may prefer Psychology, Biology or Mathematics.
Possible admission methods Class 12 marks or merit-based admission. Common entrance examination. University-specific entrance examination. Interview, counselling or document verification.

Check eligibility: Confirm accepted streams, subjects and minimum marks.
Shortlist colleges: Compare recognition, curriculum, fees and location.
Track entrance exams: Check whether merit, CUET or another test is used.
Submit applications: Prepare certificates, identification and required documents.
Confirm admission: Complete counselling, fee payment and enrolment.

Introduction to Psychology — Core ideas, approaches and applications of psychology.
Biological Psychology — Connections between the brain, body and behaviour.
Research Methods I — Observation, surveys, experiments and research ethics.
Basic Statistics — Understanding, organising and interpreting behavioural data.

Cognitive Psychology — Attention, memory, language and problem-solving.
Developmental Psychology — Human development from childhood through later life.
Social Psychology — How groups, relationships and society influence behaviour.
Research Methods II — Advanced analysis, interpretation and project preparation.

Abnormal Psychology — Introduction to psychological difficulties and classification.
Organisational Psychology — Behaviour, motivation and performance in workplaces.
Elective or Specialisation — Choose an area such as health, education or counselling.
Final Project — Conduct and present an independent research project.
Common learning activities Lectures, reading, group discussion, experiments, surveys, case analysis, presentations and supervised projects.
Common assessment methods Written examinations, assignments, presentations, research reports, practical work, viva and final projects.
Research skills Plan studies, gather information and interpret findings.
Data understanding Use basic statistics and evaluate evidence.
Critical thinking Question assumptions and compare explanations.
Communication Present ideas clearly in writing and speech.
Observation Notice patterns in behaviour and social interaction.
Ethical awareness Respect privacy, consent and responsible practice.

subsegments.subsegment: Can students from any Class 12 stream apply?

chunks.text: Many institutions accept students from Science, Commerce or Humanities. However, minimum marks, preferred subjects and entrance requirements can differ, so each institution’s latest official eligibility rules should be checked.
heading_path: Can students from any Class 12 stream apply?

chunks.text: Mathematics may not be compulsory at every institution, but the course normally includes research methods and statistics. Students should be willing to work with basic numerical data.

subsegments.subsegment: Can I become a psychologist after the bachelor’s degree?

chunks.text: A bachelor’s degree is usually the first stage. Specialised professional titles commonly require postgraduate education, supervised practical training and any applicable registration.
heading_path: Can I become a psychologist after the bachelor’s degree?

subsegments.subsegment: What is the difference between BA and BSc Psychology?

chunks.text: The exact difference depends on the university. A BSc may place more emphasis on scientific methods, biology and statistics, while a BA may include broader social-science or humanities perspectives. Always compare the actual subject list.
heading_path: What is the difference between BA and BSc Psychology?

subsegments.subsegment: Is this course suitable for someone who wants to work in HR?

chunks.text: Psychology can provide useful knowledge about behaviour, motivation and assessment. HR roles may also benefit from internships, business knowledge and specialised HR training.
